author: VW
premise: The daughter of a bishop, twenty-six and unmarried, keeps her father's household and answers his correspondence. A young curate who comes to read to the bishop treats her opinions as worth contradicting, and she finds herself, for the first time, arguing about something she cares for.
setting: A cathedral close in the west of England, 1910s

author: VW
premise: An elderly widow takes the omnibus across London to visit the house where she was born, now a boarding house. The landlady lets her look round. In each room the widow sees her mother, her brothers, and herself, and none of them notice her.
setting: Islington and the streets of north London, 1920s

author: VW
premise: A young woman who has kept house for her brother, a country doctor, since their parents died goes with him to a medical congress in Paris. At the dinners and lectures she is taken for his wife, and finds that strangers listen to her more readily than anyone at home ever has.

author: VW
premise: A young woman's first year in London, working as a typist and living in a hostel, is seen through the people who notice her in passing: a bus conductor, a clergyman's wife who runs the hostel, a young man in the office, her mother reading her letters in Yorkshire.

author: VW
premise: A woman who teaches evening classes for working men falls in love with one of her students, a printer with a wife and children. She tells no one and continues to teach him. He brings her a book he has printed himself, and she does not know what he means by it.
setting: A working men's college in Camden, London, 1910s

author: VW
premise: A woman shopping for gloves in a department store meets a friend she was at school with, now grown stout and prosperous. They have tea. Each looks at the other and sees the life she herself might have had, and neither says so.
setting: A department store in Knightsbridge, London, 1920s

author: VW
premise: A widow who lost her only son at the Somme goes each morning to feed the ducks in a London park, at the hour he used to walk there before the war. A boy of about the same age begins to sit on the next bench, and she cannot decide whether she wants him to speak.

author: VW
premise: A middle-aged Englishwoman wintering in Madeira with her invalid husband befriends a young Portuguese woman who sells lace in the hotel courtyard. Through the girl's talk of her family and her hopes, the Englishwoman sees how small and comfortable her own life has been.

author: VW
premise: A young schoolmaster from a northern industrial town spends a weekend at the country house of a pupil's family. The beauty of the house and the ease of the people enchant him, and he discovers on Sunday evening that he has been invited chiefly to make up numbers.

author: VW
premise: A woman's life from childhood to old age is glimpsed in a series of moments: a summer at the seaside, a proposal in a garden, a death in a nursing home, a walk in the park with a grandchild. The moments do not quite make a story, and she wonders whether they make a life.

author: VW
premise: A woman who has organised a charity concert spends the day of the performance soothing musicians, arranging chairs, and worrying about her husband, who has lost money and not told her. In the evening the hall fills, and she watches the faces of people she has known for twenty years.
setting: A concert hall and a house in Kensington, London, 1920s

author: VW
premise: A party of English visitors in Norway takes a steamer up a fjord to see a glacier. On board, a widower and a woman who has never married fall into a conversation that neither of them expected, while the younger members of the party quarrel about poetry.

author: VW
premise: Two sisters, one married and one not, spend a week together at the seaside with the married sister's children. The unmarried sister realises that she envies her sister nothing. The married sister realises that she envies her sister everything.

author: VW
premise: A woman travelling by train to her sister's funeral finds herself sharing a compartment with a young soldier going home on leave. They speak only of the weather and the countryside, and by the end of the journey each knows something about the other that neither has told anyone.
setting: A railway carriage between London and the north, 1916

author: VW
premise: A schoolmistress on her day off walks from her lodgings to the National Gallery, where she stands for a long time before one painting. Her thoughts move between the painting, the girls she teaches, and a letter in her bag that she has not yet opened.

author: VW
premise: A young woman who has nursed her grandmother through her last illness inherits a small legacy and spends it on a journey to Sicily alone. Her relations disapprove. In Palermo she meets no one and talks to no one, and is happier than she has ever been.

author: VW
premise: A young woman from a family of lawyers is expected to marry her father's most promising pupil. He is earnest, admiring, and rather dull. She accepts him because there is no reason not to, and spends the engagement looking for a reason.
setting: Lincoln's Inn and a house in Kensington, London, 1910s

author: VW
premise: An old schoolmaster who taught a generation of boys who went to the war sits in his empty classroom at the end of the last term before his retirement. He reads the names carved into the desks, and remembers the boys, and the boys he has forgotten.

author: VW
premise: A charwoman who cleans the offices of a firm of solicitors moves through the empty rooms early on a winter morning. She reads the letters on the desks, looks out at the river, and thinks about her son in Canada and her husband in the churchyard.
setting: An office near the Thames, London, 1920s

author: VW
premise: A pension in the south of France is full of English guests waiting out the winter: a retired governess, a young man recovering from an illness, a widow and her spinster daughter, a painter who is failing. Over a month of meals and walks, the guests settle into one another's lives.

author: VW
premise: A young woman who has spent her life looking after her widowed father announces that she intends to take rooms of her own and work for a living. Her father, a distinguished historian, is wounded and bewildered. Her aunts consider the matter a family crisis.

author: VW
premise: A crowded omnibus crosses London on a wet afternoon, and the city is glimpsed through the passengers: a typist thinking of her lover, an old man counting his change, a mother with a sick child, a clergyman composing a sermon. The bus reaches its terminus, and they scatter.
setting: An omnibus route from Hammersmith to the City, London, 1910s

author: VW
premise: A middle-aged politician walks from his club to the House of Commons on the morning of an important debate. He thinks of his speech, of his wife, of a woman he loved in his youth, and of whether any of it matters.

author: VW
premise: A young Englishwoman visiting her married sister in Italy is introduced to the circle of English artists and writers who live there. She finds them brilliant and cruel, and is drawn to the one among them who is neither.

author: VW
premise: A young man who works in a government office and writes poetry in the evenings meets, at a lecture, a young woman who works for a charity. They argue about everything. They begin to meet every week to continue the argument.

author: VW
premise: A house by the sea, rented by the same family every summer for twenty years, is seen through the summers that pass in it: children growing, parents ageing, guests coming and going, until the summer when no one comes.
setting: A house on the Cornish coast, 1890s to 1910s

author: VW
premise: A young typist on her lunch hour sits in a city churchyard eating sandwiches. She watches the pigeons and the clerks and the old men on the benches, and thinks about the young man who has asked her to the theatre, and whether she will go.
setting: A churchyard in the City of London, 1920s

author: VW
premise: A middle-aged woman who has never left England travels to Greece with her brother, a classical scholar. Among the ruins she discovers that she has a feeling for beauty her brother lacks, and that she has been living his life instead of her own.

author: VW
premise: An old lady who has been the centre of a famous literary circle is visited by a young journalist who wishes to write about her. She tells him stories that are not quite true, and watches him believe them.

author: VW
premise: A woman sorting her late mother's clothes on a winter evening finds in a coat pocket a theatre ticket from a year she cannot place. She sits on the floor among the clothes and tries to imagine the evening, and the woman her mother was before she was born.

author: VW
premise: A young doctor who has just lost his first patient walks home through the city at dawn. He passes the markets opening, the milk carts, a woman washing a step, and tries to understand what he has done and what he could not do.

author: VW
premise: A young English governess travelling with her employer's family to a villa in Spain finds herself the only person in the household who speaks the language. The family depend on her, and the villagers trust her, and she begins to feel for the first time that she belongs somewhere.

author: VW
premise: A young woman who has been engaged for a year to a dull and kind man breaks the engagement on the evening before a family dinner. She must sit through the dinner with her parents, her aunts, and her former fiancé, who has not been told.

author: VW
premise: A woman who has worked for thirty years as a housekeeper in a great house is remembered, after her death, by the family she served, the servants she ruled, and the village where she was born. Each remembers a different woman.
setting: A great house in Sussex, 1890s to 1920s

author: VW
premise: A retired colonel spends a day in his London club, reading the newspapers, eating his lunch, and talking to no one. In the afternoon he receives a telegram announcing that his son is getting married. He does not know the bride.
setting: A club in St James's, London, 1920s

author: VW
premise: A young man recovering from an illness is sent by his doctors to a hotel in the mountains of Switzerland. Among the invalids and their families he meets a young woman who is not ill at all, but who has come to escape her family.
setting: A hotel in the Swiss Alps, 1900s

author: VW
premise: A young woman who has always wanted to be a painter is told by her family that she must marry, and by her teacher that she has no talent. She paints anyway, in an attic studio she has cleared herself, and the paintings are seen by no one.

author: VW
premise: An old man sits on a bench by the sea and watches the waves. He remembers his wife, his work, his children, the war. A young couple sit down at the other end of the bench. He listens to them without meaning to.
setting: A promenade at a seaside town in Sussex, 1920s

author: VW
premise: A woman who has just been told by her doctor that she is seriously ill takes a taxi home through the city. She looks out at the streets and the people with new eyes, and decides not to tell her husband until after the dinner party that evening.

author: VW
premise: A party of English visitors to a Mediterranean island climbs a mountain on a hot afternoon. On the way, they quarrel, flirt, confide in one another, and fall silent before the view. On the way down, nothing is quite the same between them.

author: VW
premise: A young man who has been engaged to a beautiful and conventional girl finds himself drawn to her plain and unconventional friend, who works for a living and laughs at him. He does not know how to stop.
setting: London and a house in the country, 1910s

author: VW
premise: A woman's friendships with three other women, from school to old age, are seen in a series of meetings: a tea party, a wedding, a funeral, a chance encounter in a railway station. Each meeting changes what the others mean.

author: VW
premise: A young man who has come to London from the provinces to make his name as a writer spends a day walking the city, looking for a room, a job, and something to write about. By evening he has found none of them, and has seen everything.

author: VW
premise: An Englishwoman who married a Frenchman and has lived in France for twenty years returns to London for her mother's funeral. She finds that she is a stranger in her own country, and that her sisters regard her as a foreigner.
setting: London, with a life in France, 1920s

author: VW
premise: A young woman who works in a bookshop is courted by a wealthy customer who knows nothing about books. She is tempted by his kindness and his money. Her friend, a struggling poet, tells her she would be selling herself.
setting: A bookshop in Charing Cross Road, London, 1910s

author: VW
premise: A dance is held in the assembly rooms of a provincial town to raise money for the hospital. It is seen through the evening of those who attend: a girl at her first dance, a widower who has come out of duty, the band leader, a matron who watches over the punch bowl.
setting: Assembly rooms in a cathedral town, 1910s

author: VW
premise: A woman who has lived in the same London street for forty years walks its length on the day before the house is to be sold. She remembers the people who lived in each house, and the people she was when she knew them.

author: VW
premise: A young woman travelling with her father in Egypt meets a young archaeologist who is excavating a tomb. She is fascinated by his work, and by him. Her father, who wishes her to marry a cousin at home, decides to cut the journey short.

author: VW
premise: A young woman who has just come down from university returns to her parents' house and finds that nothing has changed and that she has changed completely. She must decide whether to stay and be a dutiful daughter or leave and find work.

author: VW
premise: A family is seen through the years of the war: a son at the front, a daughter in a hospital, a mother at home, a father in his office. Their letters cross, their visits fail, and at the end of the war they find they have become strangers to one another.

author: VW
premise: A young mother takes her small son to the park on a spring morning. As he plays, she thinks of her own mother, her husband, her friends, the book she meant to write, and the person she thought she would become.

author: VW
premise: A young man on a walking tour of the Alps with a friend falls in love with a young woman at an inn. His friend, who is in love with him, watches. The young woman does not notice either of them.

author: VW
premise: An old couple who have been married for fifty years give a party to celebrate. Their children and grandchildren gather. During the party, the wife slips away to the garden and thinks about the man she might have married instead.

author: VW
premise: A woman waiting for a train at a country station on a summer evening watches the other passengers and the porter and the swallows. The train is late. By the time it comes, she has decided something about her life without quite knowing what.

author: VW
premise: A young woman who works in a department store spends her day serving customers, eating her lunch in the staff room, and thinking about the young man she met at a dance. On her way home, she sees him with another girl.

author: VW
premise: An English family takes a villa on the Italian lakes for the summer. The eldest daughter falls in love with an Italian count, the youngest son runs wild in the hills, and the mother writes letters home that say nothing of what is happening.

author: VW
premise: A young woman cataloguing the library of a great house for its new owner finds the house's history written in the margins of its books: a girl's pencilled verses, a soldier's notes, a mother's list of children's illnesses. She begins to feel she knows the family better than its heir does.

author: VW
premise: A great house in the country is seen through the generations that have lived in it: a girl in the eighteenth century, a soldier home from the Crimea, a suffragette, and a young couple who must decide whether to sell it.
setting: A country house in Kent, across two centuries

author: VW
premise: On the day of a great funeral procession through London, a young clerk is sent on an errand across the city. The streets are full of mourners. He threads his way through the crowds, and the crowds become, for a moment, his own grief for someone he has never mourned.

author: VW
premise: A young woman returning to England after a year in India with her family sits on the deck of the ship as it approaches the coast. She thinks of what she has seen and what she will tell her friends, and realises that she will tell them nothing.
setting: A ship in the English Channel, 1900s
